title: Credential value under two or more stacked encodings
description: An authored base value encoded, and the resulting text encoded again, two or three times, for example hex of Base64, Base64 of Base64, or hex of hex. Layers are listed in decode order on the span, outer first. Each layer's output is ASCII text, so every layer is a valid input for the next decode step; length grows by about four thirds per Base64 layer and doubles per hex layer.
semantics: Recovering the base needs a decode step per layer, and nothing in the encoded text states how many layers there are or whether a layer is meant to be decoded. The fixtures state the layers and the decoded digest; they do not state a depth a product should decode to, a size limit or an expansion limit. Those bounds, and what happens beyond them, belong to the owning product. Single-layer questions of the same family are in credential-in-base64-or-hex-form.

applicability.rationale: Nesting is independent of the family; only the base value differs.

evidenceBasis.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 2 (#94)): when the decoded base is a credential, the whole encoded text is the range and the outcome is must-flag. Stacked layers (up to the corpus limit of three layers and 1 KB) follow the same rule as one layer; the engine's own depth limit is higher and the product's decode limits stay the product's. The benign twins (a decoded base that is not a credential) stay must-not-flag under the same policy. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: Defines each single Base64 and Base16 layer; states nothing about applying encodings repeatedly.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154).
